note: StorageCall: one row per call, addressed by its key (verb:number). Cases start a row with STORAGE_CALL_READY (what the gate hands over); the retry run starts and the first attempt signs and sends in that dispatch. StorageCall knobs (accessKeyId, pathStyle, pathPrefix, publicUrlBase) are set by the case config of the default trait. The keyed client and timeout are not default traits here, so a send stops at STORAGE_HTTP_SEND (no connect; the replay net grant knows no env host); replies are stepped on StorageHttp. Self-handled internal events (declared -> internal) are consumed by the trait and not listed. Known answers: the AWS iam example (secret wJalrXUtnFEMI/K7MDENG+bPxRfiCYEXAMPLEKEY, 20150830, us-east-1, iam: kDate hex 0138c7a6cbd60aa727b2f653a522567439dfb9f3e72b21f9b25941a42f04a7cd, kSigning hex c4afb1cc5771d871763a393e44b703571b55cc28424d1a5e86da6ed3c154a4b9, signature 5d672d79c15b13162d9279b0855cfba6789a8edb4c82c400e06b5924a6f2b5d7), the S3 header-auth GET with Range (f0e8bdb87c964420e857bd35b5d6ed310bd44f0170aba48dd91039c6036bdb41) and the S3 presigned GET (aeeed9bbccd4d02ee5c0109b86d86835f995330da4c265957d157751f604d404). Every other expected value is computed with an independent HMAC implementation over the same canonical forms.
